title: Backend mid domain caching strategies
question: Compare cache-aside and write-through caching strategies. When would you reach for each?
idealAnswer:
Cache-aside (lazy loading): application checks the cache first, on a miss reads from the database and populates the cache, writes go directly to the database and either invalidate or update the cache entry

Write-through: every write goes through the cache, which writes to the database synchronously, so the cache is always up to date and reads are guaranteed fresh, at the cost of every write paying cache-write latency

Explains staleness tradeoffs: cache-aside can serve stale data if invalidation is missed or delayed, write-through avoids that but adds write latency and complexity

Mentions cache invalidation as the hard part in practice, e.g. TTLs as a simple safety net, and the difficulty of invalidating exactly the right keys when underlying data changes

Gives a sensible use case for each: cache-aside for read-heavy data that's expensive to compute and tolerates brief staleness (e.g. product listings), write-through for data where reads must reflect the latest write immediately after it happens
